name: Tarshish
overview: Tarshish is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Javan, as recorded in Genesis 10:4. Beyond this genealogical note, the biblical text does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal history. His mention situates him within the post-Flood genealogies that trace the nations descending from Noah's sons.
namesAndTitles: The name Tarshish is a proper name possibly meaning 'yellow jasper,' 'greedy one,' or relating to a 'foundry' or 'refinery.' These meanings suggest associations with wealth or craftsmanship, though the text does not explicitly connect these to the individual himself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Tarshish as the son of Javan, establishing a direct paternal relationship in the genealogical line. No other family relationships or tribal affiliations are specified in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Tarshish's significance lies primarily in his place within the Table of Nations in Genesis 10, which outlines the descendants of Noah and the origins of various peoples. As a son of Javan, he represents one branch of the postdiluvian world’s population, contributing to the biblical understanding of the spread of nations. His mention underscores God's providential ordering of human history through genealogies.
